name: Plan arbiter — generate wide, judge, escalate the survivor
description: Fan out three cheap agents to generate competing plans for a task, a mid-tier judge picks the best, then escalate the winner to an expensive model for elaboration. Structural independence: generators are fresh Haiku sessions that never see each other; the judge is a fresh Sonnet session with no generation context; the elaborator is a fresh Opus session that only sees the winner, not the losers. Each tier does what it's best at — Haiku explores the space, Sonnet filters, Opus refines. Params: task (the work to plan for — bake in all context), cwd (working directory the agents read for codebase context). To change model tiers, edit the definition or clone it.

params.prompt:
You are a planning agent. Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the following task. Be specific: name files, functions, and the sequence of changes. Identify risks and open questions.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. No preamble. Label it PLAN-1.

meta.description: Generator 1 — Haiku, fresh session, explores one approach.

params.prompt:
You are a planning agent. Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the following task. Explore an ALTERNATIVE approach to the obvious one — consider a different decomposition, a different entry point, or a different ordering. Be specific: name files, functions, and the sequence of changes. Identify risks and open questions.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. No preamble. Label it PLAN-2.

meta.description: Generator 2 — Haiku, fresh session, prompted to explore an alternative.

params.prompt:
You are a planning agent. Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the following task. Prioritize SIMPLICITY — what is the smallest, least-risky change that fully satisfies the task? Cut scope aggressively where the task allows it. Be specific: name files, functions, and the sequence of changes. Identify risks and open questions.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. No preamble. Label it PLAN-3.

meta.description: Generator 3 — Haiku, fresh session, prompted for minimal-scope approach.

params.prompt:
You are an independent judge. Three planning agents each produced a plan for the same task. You have access to the same codebase they read. Your job: evaluate each plan against the ACTUAL code, pick the best one (or synthesize a hybrid if pieces from different plans combine well), and explain your reasoning.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

=== PLAN-1 ===
{{nodes.gen-1.result.reply}}

=== PLAN-2 ===
{{nodes.gen-2.result.reply}}

=== PLAN-3 ===
{{nodes.gen-3.result.reply}}

Evaluate each plan on: correctness (does it actually work against this codebase?), completeness (does it cover the full task?), simplicity (unnecessary complexity?), risk (what could go wrong?).

Your reply MUST follow this format:
WINNER: PLAN-N (or HYBRID)
REASONING: why this plan wins and the others lose
FINAL PLAN: the complete plan to hand to the implementer (either the winner verbatim, or the hybrid you constructed)
REJECTED: what was wrong with each losing plan

meta.description: Judge — Sonnet, fresh session, structurally independent from generators. Reads all three plans + the actual codebase.
Elaborator — Opus, fresh session. Only sees the winning plan (not the losers). Verifies against actual code and fills gaps.
